name: Midwest Woodcraft
old_description: Here at Midwest Woodcraft we have a passion for wood and working with our hands. Wood is such a special medium. It isn't fabricated, it is grown. And it has a soul. Our goal with everything we make is to discover what is hidden in the bark and highlight what took decades to produce.
about:
Midwest Woodcraft operates from Corcoran, Minnesota. The business began when its founder, after 11 years as an auto mechanic, left the trade because the physical demands had taken a toll and pursued a long‑held passion for woodworking. No founding year is published, and the owner is not named in public materials.

The shop produces custom furniture and offers a sawmilling service: it picks up downed logs, mills them into lumber or slabs, dries the wood, and builds heirloom pieces from that same material. Work shown includes dovetail‑joined drawers in soft maple, solid walnut buffets, and a quarter‑sawn white oak sewing table with a mission‑style flip‑up mechanism. An Etsy storefront sells smaller finished goods. Facility size, headcount, and annual volume are not disclosed.

Customers are primarily residential — homeowners seeking one‑of‑a‑kind pieces that fit a specific space or want to preserve a sentimental tree. The sawmilling service appeals to property owners with large trees slated for removal. No commercial or industrial sectors are cited.

The founder describes wood as a grown medium with a soul, and the goal is to reveal what decades of growth have hidden in the bark. The business was started to create pieces that friends and families gather around, turning daily work into something personally meaningful.

Mike's Welding operates from a storefront and workshop in Sterling, Alaska, with a mailing address at PO Box 627. The business has maintained a web presence since at least 2015, though the exact founding date and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed. The shop serves the local community and seasonal visitors along the Kenai Peninsula.

The shop specializes in welding and metal fabrication, with a notable seasonal focus on dip net sales and repairs for the Kenai River personal use fishery. on Fridays and operating 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on Saturdays to handle increased demand. Regular hours run Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Primary customers include participants in the Kenai River dip net fishery—both Alaska residents and non-residents—who purchase new nets or bring existing gear for repair and custom modification. The shop also addresses general welding and fabrication needs for residents and businesses in the Sterling area.

The company differentiates itself by aligning its schedule with the time-sensitive dip net season, ensuring availability when demand peaks. This seasonal responsiveness, combined with on-site fabrication capability, allows Mike's Welding to serve both immediate repair needs and custom orders for the fishery.

about:
Milford Woodworking Co operates from Milford, Massachusetts, where it has served the Northeast since 1955.

The shop produces custom cabinetry for residential and commercial projects, including kitchens, entertainment centers, desks, bookcases, bathroom vanities, china cabinets, and hutches. It also fabricates and installs laminate and solid-surface countertops, working with supplier lines such as Corian, Gibraltar, Formica, Wilson Art, and Amerock hardware. Projects move from one-on-one design consultations through fabrication and final installation, all handled in-house at the Milford facility.

Customers range from homeowners to commercial contractors across the Northeast. The company emphasizes repeat and referral business, serving clients who need tailored cabinetry and countertop solutions for new construction and remodeling.

Milford Woodworking says it differentiates itself through a commitment to honest quotes, realistic delivery dates, and standing behind every project. Its mission stresses continuous improvement, putting customer needs first, and delivering the finest quality cabinetry at an affordable price.

name: Mill Creek Packaging Inc
old_description: Keep your specialty product shipments secure with tailor-made wooden crates.
about:
Founded in 1975 in Glenview, Illinois, Mill Creek Packaging Inc began as a small operation building crates and pallets. The company relocated to its current facility in Wadsworth, Illinois in 1989, where it continues to design, build, and warehouse a range of packaging products.

Today the firm produces custom wooden crates, pallets, corrugated cartons, and foam cushioning, along with custom storage solutions such as totes, bins, and racks. Its services extend to print and artwork design, pre‑assembled packaging options, and a suite of supply‑chain programs including just‑in‑time ordering, inventory management, kanban replenishment, and warehousing. The company also offers same‑day delivery on stocked items and flexible run quantities for both domestic and export shipments.

Mill Creek serves a broad North American customer base, with noted experience in the automotive and marine sectors as well as energy equipment manufacturing. Its packaging solutions are tailored to specialty product shipments that require secure, tailored containment.

The company emphasizes personal account management and decades of hands‑on expertise as its primary differentiators, positioning itself as a partner that goes beyond standard packaging supply to provide integrated logistics support.

name: Mill Haven Foods
old_description: We are excited to offer this website to our customers and all those servicing and exploring the richness of the dairy industry.
about:
Mill Haven Foods, LLC operates from New Lisbon, Wisconsin, in the heart of the state's dairy farmland, with additional facilities in Tomah, Wisconsin. The company is a subsidiary of Select Milk and has a sister company, Select Custom Solutions, based in La Crosse, Wisconsin. While the founding year is not publicly disclosed, the business was established to serve the dairy ingredient market with custom blending and packaging solutions.

The company specializes in the research, manufacture, blending, and packaging of dry dairy food ingredients for the food and beverage industry worldwide. Its newly designed facility houses state-of-the-art blending and packaging equipment, supported by a 77,000-square-foot warehouse with allergen-control segregation and an in-house lab capable of testing fat, protein, moisture, aerobic plate count, yeast, and mold. Annual production reaches 40 million pounds, and every ingredient lot undergoes third-party purity and identity testing before use.

Mill Haven Foods serves the food and beverage, dairy, and supplement industries, providing custom blending, ingredient sourcing, private labeling, and contract manufacturing to customers worldwide. Its client base includes businesses further servicing the dairy industry, leveraging long-standing relationships with major ingredient manufacturers and distributors to secure competitive pricing and consistent protein supply.

The company emphasizes quality as its primary differentiator, maintaining NSF certification, Orthodox Union kosher certification, GMP compliance, Informed Choice program participation, and gluten-free certification through GFCO. A rigorous vendor approval program requires third-party audits and annual re-qualification, while internal QA teams conduct facility visits. Competitive pricing, stable sourcing, and a comprehensive testing regimen — both in-house and via third-party labs — underpin its value proposition.

name: Millard Manufacturing Corporation
old_description: is a stainless steel fabricator specializing in custom machinery and equipment for industrial food processing plants.
about:
Millard Manufacturing Corporation is based in La Vista, Nebraska, just outside Omaha. The privately held company was founded in 1986 and has grown into a stainless steel fabricator that designs, builds, and installs custom machinery for industrial food processing plants.

The company operates a facility of over 100,000 square feet with ten assembly bays, ten loading docks, high-bay ceilings, overhead cranes, and an automated material handling system. Its shop is equipped for laser cutting, water jet cutting, TIG/MIG welding, and an in-house passivation operation (Millard PassPro™). Engineering services include 2D/3D CAD design, cooperative design, and preliminary layout development. The company also provides factory acceptance testing, installation, and spare-parts support, and it can source raw materials such as aluminum, carbon steel, galvanized steel, and stainless steel through its affiliated Millard Metal Services.

Millard serves core food-processing sectors including beef, pork, and poultry processors, canning operations, and fresh and frozen food plants. Additional markets span animal health, bakery, dairy, pet food, pharmaceutical, prepared foods, seafood, vegetable processing, ethanol, grain milling, chemical plants, and wastewater facilities. Customers range from small operations to large corporations nationwide.

The company emphasizes its in-house passivation capacity, factory acceptance testing, and extensive stainless inventory as key differentiators. Its mission stresses timely delivery, fair treatment of employees and vendors, and adherence to current safety and sanitary design standards.

name: Miller Wire Works, Inc.
old_description: Manufacturing woven wire products since 1949 and polyurethane product since 1982
about:
Miller Wire Works, Inc. has operated in Birmingham, Alabama since its founding on April 1, 1949. The company began as a small shop with three employees under Charles E. Miller, producing woven wire partitions, guards, and folding gates. Now in its third generation of family ownership, the business remains privately held by the Miller family.

Today the company runs two manufacturing plants, a machine shop, and office space totaling 78,000 square feet with a workforce of over 50 people. Core manufacturing includes woven wire screens, polyurethane screens, rubber screens, and perforated plate. In addition to its own products, Miller Wire Works distributes a range of material‑handling components such as conveyor belting, idlers, and scrapers, as well as loader bucket protection, cutting edges, aggregate screening and crushing equipment, abrasion‑resistant steel liners, chromium‑carbide overlay, and cast‑alloy wear liners.

The primary markets served are mining, aggregate, and pulp‑and‑paper operations, along with broader material‑handling, screening, crushing, and wear‑protection applications. Customers include quarry and mine operators, aggregate producers, and industrial facilities that require custom screen media and wear‑resistant components.

The company cites its differentiators as a strict policy of honesty and integrity, wire screens woven from the highest‑quality wire for maximum wear and impact resistance, urethane products formulated from premium raw materials to customer specifications, decades of experience in the aggregate and mining sectors, and a full‑service model that combines in‑house manufacturing with a broad distribution line.

name: Min Plastics & Supply, Inc.
old_description: We help businesses, designers, and builders navigate plastic material selection, sourcing, precision cutting, fabrication, and assembly — so plastic parts and projects perform as intended.
about:
Min Plastics & Supply, Inc. was founded in 1950 by K.Y. Min in Honolulu, Hawaii. The company began as an entrepreneurial venture supplying quality acrylic products to local businesses and individuals in post-war Hawaii. Today it remains a family-owned business, operated by the second and third generations of the Min family from its facility in the Iwilei district.

The company functions as both a distributor and a fabricator. It stocks one of the largest inventories of engineered plastic sheets in the Pacific — including acrylic, polycarbonate, expanded PVC, HDPE, ABS, polypropylene, UHMW, nylon, acetal, and PETG — and runs a full-service fabrication shop equipped with CNC panel saws, CNC routers, and laser cutting and engraving systems. Services span material sourcing, cut-to-size parts, precision CNC routing, laser cutting and engraving, and custom fabrication and assembly for projects ranging from single pieces to large-scale installations.

Min Plastics serves construction, signage, marine, environmental, manufacturing, industrial, and government agencies across Hawaii, as well as specialized sectors such as maritime research, retail, and museum and art display cases. Its customer base includes commercial contractors, institutional clients, public-sector entities, designers, and builders who rely on the company for material guidance and finished components.

The firm emphasizes removing guesswork from plastics selection and fabrication. It promises quote responses within one business day, a remake-at-no-charge guarantee if cut parts deviate from quoted dimensions, and end-to-end support from material selection through installation. This approach, built over 75 years, positions the company as a local partner that combines commercial-grade inventory with Hawaii-specific logistics knowledge.

name: Minnesota Micro Molding, Machining & Manufacturing
old_description: machines with sub-micron repeatability, internal robotic pallet loading, and 24/7 lights-out capability. Both active since 2020.
about:
Minnesota Micro Molding, Machining & Manufacturing (operating as M5 Micro) was founded in 2016 in Hutchinson, Minnesota. The company began as a specialist in micro-scale molding and machining, combining both capabilities under one roof.

The shop runs micro injection molding with shot sizes from 0.0001 g to 0.6 g, processing thermoplastics and metal injection molding (MIM) materials, including overmolding, insert molding, and dual-shot (2K) operations. It also operates 5-axis micro machining on KERN Micro Vario centers with robotic pallet loading for 24/7 lights-out production, wire EDM (Mitsubishi MV1200S), small-hole EDM, and in-house metrology (Mitutoyo CMM, vision system, Starrett optical comparator). Gage-quality molds and tooling are built internally on the same 5-axis machines. The facility supports prototype through high-volume cell production.

Primary markets include medical devices (surgical tools, catheters, implant components, diagnostic cartridges, pacemaker-class parts), fiber-optic ferrules for AI compute and satellite interconnects, photonics packaging, microfluidics, drug delivery, aerospace & defense, and electronics. Customers are typically medical device OEMs and photonics manufacturers requiring tight tolerances, material traceability, and PPAP-ready documentation.

The company emphasizes its integrated "full-stack" cell: robotic part extraction, 100% in-line vision inspection every cycle, automated tray loading with per-slot traceability, and in-house heat treating and surface grinding to avoid outsourcing delays. This setup aims to deliver sub-micron repeatability and consistent unattended runs.
